name: Alyaev et al.: Direct multi-modal inversion of geophysical logs using deep learning (MDN + multiple-trajectory-prediction loss, ESS 2022) and its sequential version, Sequential multi-realization probabilistic interpretation of well logs (SPWLA 2022)
authors_org: Sergey Alyaev (NORCE Norwegian Research Centre) and Ahmed H. Elsheikh (Heriot-Watt University) for ESS 2022; S. Alyaev, A. Ambrus, N. Jahani, A. H. Elsheikh for SPWLA 2022. Funded by the DigiWells SFI (Aker BP, ConocoPhillips, Equinor, and others)
year: 2022 (arXiv preprint Jan 2022; ESS published Sep 2022; SPWLA 63rd Symposium June 2022; NFES/NORCE workshop poster Nov 2022)
venue_link: Earth and Space Science 9(9), e2021EA002186, doi:10.1029/2021EA002186 (https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2021EA002186; arXiv:2201.01871 https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.01871). SPWLA 63rd Annual Logging Symposium, Stavanger, doi:10.30632/SPWLA-2022-0112 (https://onepetro.org/SPWLAALS/proceedings-abstract/SPWLA22/SPWLA22/D051S022R001/487879). Poster: https://nfes.org/assets/workshop2022/ambrus_sequential_multi_mode_inversion_poster.pdf
code_availability: Only the MTP loss is public: PyTorch implementation 'alin256/multi-mode-prediction-with-mtp-loss' v1.2, Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.6531534 (https://zenodo.org/records/6531534), GitHub user alin256. Synthetic SVD-curve dataset: DataverseNO doi:10.18710/1F9GYH. The GWC 2020 typelog comes from Miner et al. 2021. The sequential SPWLA code is not public [uncertain]. No trained weights.
evidence_level: Peer-reviewed journal (ESS 2022, open access, full text read). SPWLA 2022 paper known only from its abstract plus the NFES 2022 poster (full paper paywalled, not read).
extreme_summary: A small CNN reads the lateral-GR minus typewell-GR difference heat map, which is the same object as our gr_abs_diff cost image, and an MDN head outputs M=7 whole stratigraphic curves plus their probabilities in one ~1.5 ms pass. It is trained with Cui et al.'s multiple-trajectory-prediction (MTP) loss: best-of-M L1 regression plus cross-entropy on the winning mode, which avoids MDN mode collapse. The SPWLA version chains windows, seeding new curves from old endpoints and merging or pruning them, so it tracks hundreds of realizations.
task_definition: Stratigraphic inversion for geosteering. Given a horizontal-well log g(x) along MD and a vertical offset-well log f(z) along stratigraphic vertical depth (SVD), find the SVD function b*(x) with f(b*(x)) = g(x): the well's stratigraphic position along MD, which is equivalent to our TVT. The model also extrapolates b(x) ahead of the data (look-ahead prediction). It outputs several likely b(x) curves and their probabilities.
inputs: Gamma ray only in ESS 2022, from the GWC 2020 semi-final synthetic typelog of the Middle Woodford (0.5 ft sampling, normalised to 0-1). The SPWLA/poster version adds rate of penetration (ROP) as a second log pair. The input is the heat map r_ij = g_j - f_i on a 64-cell (32 ft TVD) typewell window x 16 ft of observed lateral. No trajectory or inclination channels (layer-cake assumption, no dip input). No neighbour wells.
target_parameterisation: The SVD function b(x) relative to the window start: a 32-point curve (16 ft inversion over observed data plus 16 ft prediction ahead). Every second training sample is re-centred so b(0)=0, which favours continuity with the previous inversion. No explicit dip state; dip, curvature and faults are learned from the synthetic curve generator.
output_representation: K hypotheses: M whole curves (M=7 selected; 1-9 tested) plus M unnormalised log-probabilities, as one concatenated vector of size M x (l+ + 1). Each mode is a coherent path over the whole window, not a per-column marginal. No per-mode width is predicted; the kernel width is fixed implicitly by the loss weight alpha_class=0.1.
architecture: Regression head: three 3x3 Conv2D + 2x2 max-pool pairs over the normalised difference image, then two fully connected layers, all ReLU. MDN predictor: a 4096-wide dense ReLU layer and a linear output of M x (32+1) values (dense design adopted from Cui et al. 2019). Tiny by modern standards and not tuned; the authors leave hyperparameter optimisation to future work. Sequential version (poster): the network runs on consecutive windows, each previous realization's endpoint seeds the next window's inversion, coinciding endpoints merge with summed probability, low-probability branches are pruned, and hundreds of realizations are tracked, similar to beam search with learned proposals.
core_mechanism: Winner-takes-all training. Only the hypothesis closest to the truth (L1 distance over the curve) gets the regression gradient, so the M heads specialise on distinct zero-isolines of the difference image: repeated-band alternatives, dip up vs dip down, fault throws. A classification head learns how often each specialised hypothesis wins, which gives implicit probabilities learned from the frequency of geological configurations in training. Rupprecht et al. 2017 show this approximates a Voronoi-cell mixture of the conditional density. Collapse is measured, not assumed: 'collapsed modes' are pairs closer to each other than the best mode is to the truth (12.1% at M=7).
training_objective: L_MTP = L_class + alpha * L_reg (poster writes alpha on the MAE term; paper alpha_class = 0.1). m* = argmin_m ||b_m - b*||_1. L_reg = mean |b_m* - b*| (MAE, length-normalised), applied only to m*. L_class = -log softmax(p)_{m*}. Adam, lr 5e-5, batch 512, 28 M synthetic training samples, early stopping (patience 3 epochs, 4 validation checks per epoch). 5.2 h on one RTX 2080 Ti. Correlated noise (exponential kernel, correlation length 8 cells) added at train time in Section 5.5.
decoding: No single point decode is prescribed. The paper reports best-mode MAE (an oracle over modes with p >= 5%) and a mixture NLL with fixed width sigma = 3.2 cells. Downstream use is meant to be decision optimisation over the realization set. The sequential poster shows a 'predicted SVD function' line, presumably the most probable path [uncertain]. A probability-weighted mean of the M paths is possible but not evaluated.
metric_consistent_decode: Not RMSE-consistent as published. The reported numbers are oracle best-of-M; picking the highest-probability mode is mode-seeking; the per-mode L1 loss is median-like. A probability-weighted mean of the M curves approximates the posterior mean (RMSE-optimal) only if the mode probabilities are calibrated. The paper's bucketed reliability check shows this roughly holds up to about P35 and drifts above that.
evidence_scope: Local window: 16 ft of lateral and a 32 ft typewell window per evaluation. The sequential version accumulates evidence along the lateral only through realization bookkeeping (endpoint seeding, merge and prune), not through a learned long-range receptive field.
prefix_conditioning: Implicit. Each window starts from the endpoint of a previous realization (half the training samples are centred at 0), so the known start acts as an anchor. There is no fine-tuning or closed-form correction from known heel labels.
propose_vs_select: Propose. It emits M candidate paths with scores in one pass, so it fits naturally as a candidate generator for a downstream reranker, gate or decision optimiser. The sequential version adds a hand-coded select step (merge and prune by probability).
physical_constraints: Layer-cake assumption: the log depends only on SVD position; constant thickness; faults and dips only as represented in the synthetic curve generator. Geological plausibility is learned from the data prior, not enforced. No ordering, smooth-dip or TVT + Z identity constraints.
dataset: Fully synthetic. 28 M training triples, 12 k validation, 10 k test: a random 64-cell section of the GWC 2020 semi-final typelog (Middle Woodford, South-Central Oklahoma), a random SVD curve with trend 0, and the lateral log generated by linear interpolation of the typelog along the curve. Extra hand-made scenarios: flat, slope (82/98 deg), fault (3.75 ft throw). The SPWLA/poster version uses GWC 2020 GR + ROP with realistic stratigraphy and a fault at 2750 ft MD.
synthetic_to_real: 100% synthetic, with a single typelog; the lateral log is an exact resample of the offset log (noise-free in the reference model). Section 5.5 shows the model is brittle: the 0%-noise model falls below the constant baseline once test noise exceeds about 2%. Training with 10% correlated noise gives robustness past the 6-7% GWC noise standard, at the cost of 'trusting' the data less. No lateral-vs-typewell GR normalisation or bias mismatch is modelled, and there is no real-data alignment stage.
metric_and_performance: ESS 2022 test set (cells of 0.5 ft): best-mode MAE 2.34 cells for M=1 (deterministic) vs 1.13 for M=7, i.e. a 52% reduction; 1.60 for M=2, 1.32 for M=3. Mixture NLL is lowest for M=1 (0.365; single-mode predicts averages), and the well-log NLL is best for M=2 and M=7. Fault scenario best-mode MAE 3.08 (M=1) vs 1.40 (M=7). With 1% noise: 5.67 (M=1) vs 2.75 (M=7). Constant-zero baseline: 6.04 cells. Inference 1.5 ms per window. Sequential GWC case (poster): tracks the true curve through a fault, 443 ms total on a standard PC; no RMSE given.
comparability: Low. The numbers are oracle best-of-M MAE in 0.5 ft cells over 32-ft windows (half of which is extrapolation) on synthetic single-typelog data. They are not pooled RMSE of a deployable decode over whole real laterals. The only transferable fact is the relative gain of best-of-M over deterministic (about 2x), which mirrors our own oracle best-mode gap (4.84 deployed vs 4.27 oracle on the 60-ep model).
validation_protocol: Random synthetic train/val/test splits generated with the same rules and the same typelog, so there is no spatial or well grouping and no real-well holdout. The fault/slope/flat scenarios are hand-constructed probes. Calibration is checked with probability-bucket reliability on validation and test.
inference_budget: About 1.5 ms per window on GPU for ESS; 443 ms for a whole GWC lateral including sequential bookkeeping on a standard PC. Far inside the Kaggle budget; a K-path head added to our U-Net would cost essentially nothing at inference.
repeated_layers: The paper's core target. The difference image shows several zero-isolines (e.g. four modes, symmetric around 0 and around 4 ft); separate MTP heads lock onto different isolines, and the classifier ranks them by learned geological frequency. Failure mode shown: the correct band is often not the highest-probability mode (p = 8% and 17% in the worked examples). Even a perfect multi-hypothesis generator leaves the selection problem, which is exactly our wrong_mode + multimodal_miss share.
drift: Handled only through the synthetic curve prior (learned dip up vs down, curvature) and through look-ahead extrapolation. There is no explicit dip state or straight-line drift correction. The re-centring trick favours continuity from the previous endpoint, which can also propagate drift.
uncertainty_and_calibration: Mode probabilities come from a softmax cross-entropy on the winning index. A reliability analysis over probability buckets (P0-P10 ... P30+) shows good agreement below about P35 and deviation above, within error bars because the high buckets have few samples. No temperature scaling or ECE. Mode width is fixed, not predicted. Collapse rate is reported per M (2.3% at M=2 up to 15.1% at M=9); M was chosen as the largest M whose collapse rate stays below 1/M.
where_to_use: (1) As an auxiliary K-path head on the ConvNeXt/FastViT decoder: K whole-lateral TVT curves (345 columns) plus K logits trained with MTP alongside the existing per-column softmax loss. (2) As a candidate generator for a whole-lateral reranker scoring each path by full-lateral GR misfit, prefix consistency and single-straight-line drift, which is what our failed per-point gates could not see. (3) As a structured source of mode-level calibration for a probability-weighted mean decode. (4) The sequential merge/prune bookkeeping as a beam-search alternative to our post-hoc forward-backward decode.
error_mode_targeted: Band confusion (wrong_mode 24%, multimodal_miss 12%, blend 15%): about 51% of squared error. Secondary: faulted or broad-hump cases.
gap_vs_our_implementation: What we already have: the input representation is effectively identical (their r_ij = g - f heat map is our gr_abs_diff/gr_signed_diff cost image, and ours adds 14 more channels), and our 400-bin per-column softmax is strictly more expressive per column than 7 Gaussian-less modes. So the per-column representation is not the gap. What we lack: (a) path-level (joint) hypotheses. Our softmax gives marginals per MD column, so we have no object that says 'band A along the whole lateral, with probability p'. Per-point RMSE with a calibrated marginal is already Bayes-optimal, so the benefit is not a better decode of the same posterior. It is a training signal and a selection interface: MTP forces coherent whole-path alternatives, and a whole-lateral reranker can then use evidence that per-point gates did not see (GR misfit integrated over the full lateral, drift linearity, prefix match). (b) Explicit mode probabilities with a measured collapse rate and a reliability check at mode level; our calibration is only at bin level. (c) Winner-takes-all diversity pressure. Our cross-entropy on per-column bins rewards hedged blends (the 15% blend error), whereas MTP rewards committing. Confirmation: the 2nd-place AnchorCNN + DP carries multiple level hypotheses via P(dTVT|TVT), which is related but per-level rather than per-path. Our oracle best-mode (4.27 vs 4.84 ft) quantifies the ceiling of a perfect selector over modes, and Alyaev reports the same kind of oracle-only win.
proposed_experiment: E1 (cheap, diagnostic, no training): from existing posterior dumps (seq_NN_posterior_dump.py --save-all), extract per-well top-K coherent paths by K-best Viterbi or by clustering per-column modes into band-consistent tracks (posterior_fb_decode.py already has the forward-backward machinery). Measure oracle-best-path RMSE vs oracle per-point best-mode (4.27) vs deployed expectation. If path-level oracle is not clearly below expectation, stop. E2 (main): add an MTP head to experiments/arch/seq_NN_models.py (and seq_NN_trf_unet.py for FastViT). Pool the decoder feature map over the TVT axis into a per-column feature, apply a small 1D conv/transformer along MD, and output K=4,6,8 curves of 345 TVT values (parameterised as offsets from the current expectation or from the last known heel TVT) plus K logits from a globally pooled vector. Loss in seq_NN_train.py: existing column CE + lambda * [best-of-K L2 on masked unknown columns + CE on the winner], with lambda in {0.1, 0.3} and L2 (not L1) so each mode tends to the conditional mean. Optionally use annealed or relaxed WTA (epsilon=0.05 to non-winners) against collapse. Config flag in seq_NN_cfg.py (mtp_k, mtp_lambda). Decodes: (i) unchanged expectation from the softmax head (does the auxiliary loss alone help?), (ii) probability-weighted mean of K paths, (iii) 50/50 blend. Control: same config with mtp_lambda=0, same seed(s), 150 epochs, evaluated with seq_NN_holdout_eval.py on the 155 holdout wells. Given the +-0.39 ft single-run noise floor, use at least 2 seeds per arm or seq_NN_robust_compare.py. Log the collapse rate and mode reliability on OOF. E3 (conditional on E1/E2 showing oracle headroom): a whole-lateral reranker (logistic or LightGBM) over the K paths with per-path features: integrated GR misfit, prefix agreement, straight-line drift residual, mode logit. Train on OOF only, and output soft weights for a weighted mean, not a hard pick.
implementation_effort: Medium. The head and loss are about 150 lines and the Zenodo MTP loss can be adapted. The work is in the path parameterisation over masked or unknown columns, evaluation plumbing and multi-seed runs. E1 is low effort.
gpu_cost: The head adds under 5% FLOPs. Training cost is the same as a baseline run (about the cost of our 150-epoch ConvNeXt run on the RTX 5060 8 GB); two arms x 2 seeds is about 4 baseline runs. Inference cost is negligible. E1 is CPU only.
distillation_compatibility: Good. The student can copy the K logits (KL on the softmax over modes) and the K curves (L2 after Hungarian or identity matching, since the heads are index-stable once trained). Alternatively, render the K paths plus probabilities into a per-column mixture and add it to the existing posterior KD target. The student's own softmax head is unchanged.
error_correlation_with_ours: Moderate. It shares the backbone and input channels, so errors in the evidence stay correlated; the diversity comes from path-level commitment vs hedged marginals. As a blend member it is most useful where the softmax blends two bands (the blend 15%), and least useful for drift.
risk: (1) It does not add evidence. Per the metric fact in our context, band-confusion error falls only via more evidence or better calibration, and MTP helps only if the whole-path structure or reranker extracts evidence the U-Net ignores. (2) The published gains are oracle best-of-M; the deployable decode (highest-probability mode) picked the wrong band in 2 of 3 worked examples. (3) Learned gates and selectors already failed three times (per-point ConvNeXt/AnchorCNN gate, XY geo-prior pick, forward-backward continuity), and the 3rd-place CV-to-private gap (5.29 to 5.84) warns about selection overfitting. (4) Mode collapse and heads idling (12% at K=7). The auxiliary loss can hurt the main head at 60 epochs, as happened with AcfNet, axial attention and RAFT. (5) Real laterals are much longer than 16 ft windows and have prefix labels, so K fixed paths over 345 columns may need too many modes to cover per-segment band switching.
notes: A09 is the closest in-domain predecessor of a multi-hypothesis head and uses the same difference-image input as our cost volume, so it validates the idea but not its RMSE value. The honest reading is that the paper shows multi-modality exists and can be enumerated cheaply; it does not show that enumeration improves a point estimate. For us the decisive quantity is the gap between oracle-best-path and expectation on real holdout wells (E1) before any training. The sequential merge/prune scheme is a hand-coded particle filter with learned proposals, which links to A05 (PF) and B06 (differentiable PF). Related transferable work: B04 (annealed/resilient MCL fixes WTA collapse and gives calibrated scores), B03 (multimodal stereo decoding). Poster title reference: 'AI-based multi-modal interpretation of logs for ahead-of-bit probabilistic ROP prediction' (Ambrus et al., NFES 2022).
